scope: Explicit renewal of restored aggregate paid claims, with closed unrelated-journal inspection and unchanged generic recovery fences.
assessment: Inspection distinguishes aggregate-claim-review from local pre-proof-review and no longer passes an unrelated completed predecessor to replacement inspection. It creates no signed-transaction or send permit.

The narrow path requires pre-proof state, supported local lifecycle, a valid current epoch, no current-operation signed candidate or recorded current txHash, aggregate ETH/USDC custody, same receipt triple and retained Bok claim, plus exact predecessor commitment and canonical acknowledgment.

Renewal rederives and authenticates original collateral/Bok/FPC bridge claims, synchronizes PXE, preserves saved action/nonce/encoded arguments, and uses existing strict native estimation before the exact CAS. Funding fee bridge identity is now persisted for all bridge-payment actions and compared again at final submission.

Original preproof history is retained; explicit reviewed attempt uses the current epoch. Epoch changes during estimation, changed ciphertext/predecessor, stale context and signed attempts remain closed. No journals are reset, no Ethereum payment is repeated and no balance-only fallback is introduced.

At-most-one canonical charge relies on deterministic FPC bridge nullifier insertion during nonrevertible setup in both supported fee modes, and native duplicate-nullifier rejection/transaction checkpoint rollback, as documented in diagnosis-aggregate-paid-claim-recovery.json.
Panel copy accurately distinguishes restored claim review from evidence of a locally retained unsigned attempt; renewed fee review and a separate confirmation are required.
failureScenariosChecked: ordinary restored/missing/unsupported provenance with completed predecessor stays unknown
missing or wrong aggregate custody and mixed receipt fail
changed collateral or fee claim fails
spent bridge estimation fails without CAS/send
bridge leaf changed after review fails before submission
existing late-proof, journal, broadcast, preference and read-marker context fences remain effective
limits: Focused application checks use real encrypted journals/native hashing with labelled provider, simulation and proof doubles; the spent-bridge rejection is a simulation double supported by independent native/contract source analysis.
Browser checks use labelled UI doubles. No live proof, service, payment or claim was performed.
An application-phase revert can retain setup consumption and fees; the change does not promise successful recovery of an already consumed bridge or manufacture aggregate success.
Actual original paid-claim acceptance remains required after deployment.
